Better answers start with the semantic model.

A practical recap of conversational analytics, Copilot context, AI readiness, governance, and how trusted semantic models help insurance teams move from questions to action.

Talk to Your Insurance DataFeatured speaker: Amol ManochaFabric & Power BI Insurance User Group
Meeting recap

For everyone who could not attend

Our second meeting paired community announcements with a detailed demonstration of how model design, metadata, security, and AI preparation shape the quality of conversational analytics.

The discussion moved from report-scoped Copilot to app- and service-level experiences, then into verified answers, AI instructions, schema curation, read-only validation, and practical authoring with Skills for Fabric.

What we explored

From chat with your data to trusted answers

Context changes the experience

Report, app, and service experiences provide different scopes. Supplying the intended report or workspace context helps the experience find the correct source.

Security remains foundational

The session emphasized that access is evaluated through the requesting user and that existing row-level and object-level security continue to matter.

Verified answers support consistency

Common business questions can be connected to trusted visuals so users receive a repeatable answer and can inspect the path behind it.

Descriptions carry business meaning

Descriptions help distinguish similar fields, explain date roles, and give AI better context for measures, dimensions, filters, and intended use.

Core takeaway

AI readiness is model readiness.

Reliable conversational analytics depends on the governed semantic layer beneath the experience: defined measures, meaningful descriptions, intentional schema exposure, AI instructions, verified answers, model relationships, and the security already protecting the data.

Curate

Use business-friendly names, descriptions, relationships, and deliberate field visibility.

Guide

Provide instructions, terminology, trusted routes, and answer boundaries.

Validate

Test business questions, inspect logic, and separate model checks from conversational validation.

Reusable resource

Semantic-model agentic AI readiness scorecard prompt

Replace the workspace and semantic-model placeholders, then paste the prompt into a properly configured VS Code or GitHub Copilot environment.

Scorecard Report Prompt
Certification: [certification]

Assess the AI and agentic readiness of the Power BI semantic model i want this to be:

- Workspace: "Enter workspace"
- Semantic model: "Enter Semantic model"

Before starting:

1. Review the latest guidance in the public Microsoft repository:
   https://github.com/microsoft/skills-for-fabric

2. Check whether the current Microsoft skills-for-fabric package is available in this VS Code environment. Use the latest applicable guidance from:
   - semantic-model-authoring
   - semantic-model-ai-readiness
   - semantic-model-consumption
   - FabricIQ
   - Fabric IQ ontology guidance, where relevant

3. If the required skills or MCP servers are not installed or configured, do not substitute assumptions or silently continue with a reduced assessment. Explain what is missing and guide me through installing or configuring it.

4. If Microsoft Fabric, FabricIQ, or Power BI authentication is required, open or initiate the supported sign-in flow and pause so I can authenticate.

Perform a read-only assessment. Do not modify the semantic model, report, workspace, permissions, AI configuration, or other Fabric resources unless I explicitly authorize changes afterward.

Inspect the live semantic model and assess these six dimensions using the following weights:

- Model architecture: 25%
- Business-friendly naming: 15%
- Descriptions and semantic metadata: 15%
- AI instructions: 20%
- AI data schema: 15%
- Verified Answers: 10%

The assessment should include:

1. Model foundation
   - Tables, visible and hidden columns, explicit measures, and relationships
   - Fact and dimension grains
   - Relationship cardinality and filter direction
   - Date dimensions, date roles, hierarchies, and time behavior
   - Data types, formatting, summarization, hidden technical fields, and default labels
   - Implicit versus explicit measures
   - Duplicate, overlapping, helper, or potentially misleading objects

2. Business semantics
   - Business-friendly names
   - Ambiguous terminology, abbreviations, synonyms, and conflicting definitions
   - Description coverage and quality for visible tables, columns, and measures
   - Grain, units, filters, time basis, exclusions, and denominator definitions
   - Misalignment between names, descriptions, synonyms, instructions, and actual DAX

3. AI preparation
   - Existing AI instructions and whether they provide metric routing, date defaults, clarification rules, answer boundaries, polarity, and visualization preferences
   - AI data schema scope, dependencies, synonyms, technical noise, and missing business metrics
   - Existing Verified Answers, representative coverage, filters, trigger phrases, and potential conflicts
   - Distinguish curated AI metadata from generated, suggested, legacy, or inaccessible metadata

4. Agentic-readiness controls
   - Whether named entities can be resolved to canonical model values before applying filters
   - Ambiguous-name, alias, misspelling, duplicate-name, and no-match behavior
   - Answer precedence among Verified Answers, AI instructions, descriptions, and generated DAX
   - Grounding quality and whether ontology-based grounding would provide value
   - Clarification behavior for ambiguous metrics or date roles
   - Behavior for unsupported, causal, regulated, or potentially misleading questions
   - Whether unrelated model deployments preserve existing Prep-for-AI artifacts

5. Evidence validation
   - Run a small number of safe, read-only DAX queries to verify important totals, metric definitions, date behavior, denominators, and identified ambiguities
   - Reconcile mutually exclusive categories where appropriate
   - Report actual results and distinguish model-consistency checks from source-system or accounting validation
   - Do not treat passing DAX queries as proof of conversational accuracy or as Verified Answers
   - Do not expose sensitive row-level data

6. Testing recommendations
   - Provide at least five representative business questions
   - Provide negative and ambiguous tests
   - Include tests for entity resolution, date ambiguity, unsupported metrics, causal questions, and Verified Answer near-matches
   - State what was tested, what was not tested, and what requires live Copilot or data-agent validation

Scoring rules:

- Score each dimension from 0–100 using observed evidence.
- Calculate the overall score using the stated weights and round only once at the end.
- Label the result “Indicative readiness.”
- Explain that it is a judgment-based assessment, not certification or measured conversational accuracy.
- Use 0 only when an artifact or capability is confirmed absent from an inspected source.
- If evidence is inaccessible, show “Not assessed” rather than assuming it is absent. Do not silently reweight the score; report an incomplete assessment and identify the missing evidence.
- Do not give Verified Answer credit merely because measures or DAX queries work.
- Keep agentic-readiness considerations separate from the six weighted dimensions unless the repository guidance explicitly adds them to the scoring model.

Deliverable:

Create a new, self-contained HTML file in the current VS Code workspace named:

[semantic-model-name]-agentic-ai-readiness-scorecard.html

The HTML must:

- Work offline with inline CSS and SVG
- Use a polished emerald/mint executive design
- Include a circular readiness gauge
- Include all six dimension scores
- Show four evidence-backed model inventory metrics
- Include one model-specific evidence visualization
- Identify the three highest-value improvements
- Include a “Preserve what works” section
- Include an agentic-readiness lens covering grounding, resolution, routing, answer precedence, boundaries, and change safety
- Include detailed appendices with evidence, scoring rationale, validation results, test questions, negative tests, limitations, and source links
- Clearly separate observed findings from recommendations and untested behavior
- Be responsive on desktop and mobile
- Be formatted for printing to PDF on landscape Letter paper
- Keep the executive scorecard on page 1 and place detailed appendices on subsequent pages
- Avoid blank or nearly blank PDF pages
- Include a Print / Save PDF button
- Contain no credentials, access tokens, raw sensitive records, or unnecessary connection details

Before completing:

- Verify the weighted-score arithmetic independently.
- Check all counts and findings against the inspected model.
- Confirm there is no stale content copied from another assessment.
- Test desktop and narrow mobile layouts for horizontal overflow.
- Test the evidence appendix and keyboard focus behavior.
- Test the print layout and confirm the footer stays on page 1.
- Confirm the executive page and each appendix fit within their intended printed pages.
- State whether any semantic-model or Fabric changes were made.

At the end, provide:
- A link to the generated HTML file
- The indicative score or incomplete-assessment status
- The three most important findings
- Any authentication, access, or runtime limitations
- A clear statement that the assessment was read-only
The prompt requests a read-only assessment and a self-contained HTML scorecard.
Frequently asked questions

Questions raised during the session

Do I need a fully completed semantic model before using these techniques?

No. The demonstration showed that AI-assisted authoring can be useful while a model is still developing, including drafting descriptions, proposing measures, and identifying readiness gaps. Human review and business validation remain important.

How can Copilot understand business meaning instead of only producing technically valid output?

Curate the semantic layer. Use precise measure definitions, descriptions, instructions, terminology, verified answers, and explicit date and filter behavior. Correct misunderstandings and preserve that business context with the model.

How are permissions respected?

The discussion described a user-context approach: the experience works within the requesting user's access. Existing semantic-model controls such as row-level and object-level security remain part of the access path.

Should important claim or customer knowledge remain only in email?

No. Dean raised the governance risk of critical operational knowledge remaining in individual communications. AI can help locate permitted context, but shared business records should still be maintained in the appropriate enterprise system.

What is the role of verified answers?

Verified answers provide a curated route for representative questions and trusted visuals. A successful DAX query by itself should not be treated as a verified answer or proof of conversational accuracy.

Why do some users see different Copilot entry points?

Jennifer and Amol discussed that the available experience can vary with tenant configuration, licensing, and feature rollout. The enablement and release-status links above are the best starting points for administrators.
